analysis.title: Blue Wave: Democrats sweep the US midterms
key_insights: Democrats gained control of both the House and the Senate in the US midterms held this week, ending unified Republican control of the government. The bank expects gridlock and advises investors not to overreact and to stay invested.

Equity view: stay invested and keep diversifying into more defensive sectors. The bank expects 8-10% annual S&P returns in the mid-cycle phase, down from 20.5% in the Jan 2023 to Jan 2027 early-cycle phase.

Fiscal expansion is likely to stall. Democrats can block new tax cuts and spending from the Trump administration, and Trump can veto Democratic proposals. The debt ceiling returns as an issue in H2 2027 and could bring back government shutdowns, though the bank expects compromise to prevail.

Trump keeps control of foreign policy. The bank sees a risk that the US and Israel restart combat operations with Iran now that their elections are over. Congress may limit the duration by withholding funding next year, and new tariffs may be harder to introduce under Democratic oversight.

Democrats won the Texas and Georgia governor races. Both are large data centre states and permits are largely decided at state level, so data centre moratoriums could grow in 2027. Regulation of AI model development would still need Trump's signature.

Market reaction: stocks recovered strongly from pre-market lows after Trump's conciliatory response. Defensive stocks, clean energy (solar), affordability-related names, tariff-rollback beneficiaries and Medicaid-related stocks outperformed. Semiconductors stayed weak on data centre moratorium concerns.
The bank downgraded semiconductors last month and holds a lower allocation than in September. Its AI capex estimates are below consensus, and it advises investors to stay selective.

FX: DXY near-term support is 100.7 and the 12-month target is 98.5. A Democratic sweep reduces the legislative path for tariff escalation and fiscal expansion, which supported the dollar in 2026. The effect is expected to be modest and short-lived unless Friday's non-farm payrolls report is weak. The bank sees the Fed narrative as the dominant medium-term driver.

Rates: the bank expects two more Fed hikes by H1 2027 because inflation is sticky and the economy is robust. The hiking cycle ends in Q2 2027, and markets begin pricing a cut in H2 2027. Intermediate Treasury yields fell the most after the election, and 30-year yields fell less.

The bank considers the downshift in ultra-long yields overdone given the fiscal trajectory. It recommends that investors who went long at 20-30 year maturities reduce those positions, after its late-September call to go long 10-year Treasuries.

Credit: prefer investment grade corporates at 3-7 year maturities. Slower AI data centre build-out could ease supply pressure from hyperscaler bond issuance, but data centre-focused deals could become less viable and the bank is cautious on lower-quality names in that sector.
High yield spreads have widened, with BB and B spreads resilient and CCC spreads at distressed levels. Income investors are advised to stay in the BBB-BB range.

Oil: a short-term spike is possible if combat operations in Iran restart. The bank expects WTI to drift toward its 12-month target of USD 80 per barrel as supply chains adapt and Congress restrains defense spending. It is also watching possible new Democratic regulation of US shale.

Gold: the bank stays Overweight. It sees the change in congressional control as having only a marginal effect. Central bank buying led by China and resilient investor demand have eased gold's sensitivity to real yields.

sector_views.rationale: Downgraded last month, with a lower allocation than in September. Data centre moratorium risk and a possible reset in data centre spending expectations.
The bank continues to diversify equity exposure into defensive sectors as the cycle moves to mid-cycle, and defensive stocks have held up after the election.
Listed as a new opportunistic idea (12-Oct-26). Medicaid-related stocks are rising on expected policy changes.
Solar stocks were among the biggest winners after the election, as themes favoured by Democrats outperformed. The bank gives no formal rating.
Change in congressional control has only a marginal impact. Central bank buying led by China and resilient investor demand continue.

risk_factors: Renewed US and Israel combat operations with Iran could cause an oil price spike.
The US debt ceiling and possible government shutdowns in H2 2027.
Data centre moratoriums at state level could cut AI capex and weigh on semiconductors and US equity outperformance.
A weaker-than-expected non-farm payrolls report could deepen dollar weakness.
Possible new Democratic regulation of the US shale oil industry.
CCC credit spreads at distressed levels and wide dispersion within high yield.
vol_and_positioning: VIX initially rose more than 10% in pre-market trading after the results and eased from its intraday highs after Trump's comments.
The bank says the overnight correction shows how complacent investors had become, after recent weakness in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq.
geopolitical: The bank sees a risk that the US and Israel restart combat operations with Iran after concluding their elections.
Congress may limit any renewed hostilities next year by withholding funding under Democratic control.
New US tariffs on trading partners may be harder to introduce with Democratic oversight.
Iran has made recent diplomatic overtures, but the bank still sees a short-term oil spike risk.

tension_points.bull_case: Trump's conciliatory response helped markets recover strongly from pre-market lows, and mid-cycle equities still deliver 8-10% annual returns, as in 2015-2017.
tension_points.bear_case: The overnight correction showed investor complacency. Political headwinds are typical of mid-cycle, and semiconductors face data centre moratorium risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A weaker-than-expected non-farm payrolls report on Friday would compound the dollar's decline beyond a modest, short-lived election effect.
